$comment: Enumerated disagreements between the six per-vocabulary JSON-LD contexts and the ontologies and shapes they describe, for scripts/check-context-agreement.py. This file is a GATE INPUT, not a filter: the check still examines every term and prints every finding. The run fails when a finding appears that is not listed here AND when a listed finding stops occurring (reported STALE), so the file can only SHRINK, and shrinking it is an explicit committed edit. Keys are <context file>:<term>:<finding class>; the value records what the ontology or shape said against what the context said at the time the entry was cut. Nothing here is acceptable in the long run: every entry is a place where a published dictionary misdescribes the graph a consumer writing that JSON will produce.
$rule: The ontologies and shapes are normative for the JSON to RDF mapping (D-CONTEXT-1 C1); a context that disagrees is the defect, and the cure is to fix the context, never to relax the vocabulary. Adding an entry here to make a build green is a committed admission of a published mismatch. structured-term-unscoped is the exception in one respect only: it cannot be fixed term-by-term, because it needs the JSON-LD 1.1 move to type-scoped contexts (C4), which lands one vocabulary per PR.
$established: 2026-09-05, cut from the first run of the check against the contexts as published. It measures the under-specification D-CONTEXT-1 C6 exists to resolve and does not itself fix any of it. The 52 key-not-local-name entries were added on the same date the class landed, with the class itself: the gate lands before the renames so that no new key of that shape can be added while the existing ones are worked through (D-CONTEXT-1 C2). The two container-vs-cardinality entries it replaced, cascade:involvedResources and health:monitoredVitalSigns, were removed when the check learned that an rdf:List range published as "@container": "@list" is one node and not an array the shapes reject.
